va_strawberry_fields.season: good in cold weather; avoid May-Sep

wa_ephemeral.season: Summer only, and typically not dry until late summer
wa_ephemeral.best_season: This wall holds moisture longer than most of the crag and doesn't fully dry out until late summer; plan for July through September, later than nearby left-side routes, for best conditions.

wa_iceman.season: Summer — a shaded destination good for hot days when nearby Mazama crags are too warm.
wa_iceman.best_season: Late June through September, matching the broader Washington Pass climbing season; the Ice Box's shaded, north-facing character keeps it cooler than sunnier Washington Pass walls and can hold wet rock or residual snow later into the early season.

wa_route_c.season: Summer — a shaded destination good for hot days when nearby Mazama crags are too warm.
wa_route_c.best_season: Late June through September, matching the broader Washington Pass season; the Ice Box's shaded character keeps it cooler and can hold wet rock later into early season than sunnier walls nearby.

wa_route_d.season: Summer — a shaded destination good for hot days when nearby Mazama crags are too warm.
wa_route_d.best_season: Late June through September, matching the broader Washington Pass season; the Ice Box's shaded character keeps it cooler and can hold wet rock later into early season than sunnier walls nearby.

wa_mount_rainier_curtis_ridge.season: Best in cold, stable conditions when rockfall is frozen in place; considered dangerous in warm/melting conditions

wa_mount_rainier_emmons_glacier.season: Late May (when the White River Road opens) through August, before summer melt exposes an unnavigable maze of crevasses
wa_mount_rainier_emmons_glacier.best_season: Late May through July is ideal — filled-in crevasses and good snow. By August the glacier is broken and route-finding gets complex.

wa_mount_rainier_fuhrer_finger.season: Best climbed early (spring) with a very early start each day to minimize rockfall exposure in the couloir

wa_mount_rainier_ingraham_direct.season: Typically climbed January through end of May, often under winter-like conditions, before the Disappointment Cleaver route opens up for the summer
wa_mount_rainier_ingraham_direct.best_season: Winter through May, while the Ingraham headwall is filled and continuous. By June the direct usually breaks into crevasses and the bergschrund opens — parties switch to the Disappointment Cleaver.

wa_mount_rainier_ptarmigan_ridge.season: Often in good condition by May, but the Mowich Lake road frequently doesn't open until early July, delaying that approach option

wa_mount_rainier_willis_wall.season: Almost exclusively attempted in winter/early spring cold, when serac activity is most likely to be frozen and quiescent
wa_mount_rainier_willis_wall.best_season: Late spring in cold, frozen conditions

wa_ne_couloir.season: Best in June while snow is continuous; degrades to scree/dirt by mid-late summer
wa_ne_couloir.best_season: June through early July when snow is continuous but before it retreats entirely; snow melts fairly early in the summer once roads are accessible.

wa_northeast_ridge_1963_route.season: Summer, when the low couloir approach still holds climbable snow
wa_northeast_ridge_1963_route.best_season: Late June through September, once the road is open and the lower couloir approach has consolidated snow.

wa_storm_king_southwest_scramble.season: July through the first significant snowfall of autumn (typically into October); expect lingering snow into early August in shaded sections
wa_storm_king_southwest_scramble.best_season: Late July through September is the reliable window. Snow often lingers in the basin above ~7,400 ft into early August, so carry an ice axe (and consider crampons) even for a nominally dry climb. The route generally stays climbable until the first real snows of autumn, typically early-to-mid October, but shorter days and colder nights make late-season attempts riskier given the 3-day approach.
